title: Fibre of a topos point as a filtered colimit over pointed site objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism, that is, an adjunction $p^{-1}\dashv p_*$ with $p^{-1}$ preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. For $T\in\mathcal C$ put $L_p(T)=p^{-1}(h_T^\#)$, where $h_T(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)$ and $(-)^\#$ is sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Write $\mathcal N_p$ for the category of pairs $(T,a)$ with $a\in L_p(T)$, an arrow being $b:T\to T'$ with $L_p(b)(a)=a'$. Then $\mathcal N_p$ is small and cofiltered. For every commutative ring $\Lambda$ and every sheaf $F$ of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\Lambda_{\mathcal C}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_{(T,a)\in\mathcal N_p^{\mathrm{op}}}F(T)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ p^*_{\Lambda}F$$
is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules, natural in $F$. Here $p^*_{\Lambda}$ is the constant-coefficient inverse image [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], and the map sends a section $s:h_T^\#\to F$ and $a$ to $p^{-1}(s)(a)$ on underlying sets. The functor $p^*_{\Lambda}$ is exact. Colimits of $\Lambda$-modules indexed by $\mathcal N_p^{\mathrm{op}}$ are exact; these assertions remain true after replacing $\mathcal N_p$ by any small full initial subcategory.

source.place: Tags 00YA (lemma-point-site-topos), part (2), and 00Y8 (lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf); cofilteredness from finite limits of the fibre functor, and constant-module inverse image as specified by the cited lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image. Intrinsic site-point colimit and exactness also Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Point/Basic.lean:69-97,139-147,277-291 and Point/Skyscraper.lean:222-235,295-297.

proof.text: The representable functor $T\mapsto h_T$ preserves finite limits: at each $V$, its limit comparison is the bijection between maps from $V$ into a limit and compatible families of maps. Sheafification preserves finite limits by the cited theorem, and $p^{-1}$ does so by hypothesis. Thus $L_p$ preserves the terminal object, binary products and equalizers. Its values are sets in the chosen universe, so the disjoint union of the $L_p(T)$ over the small object set, and the sets of arrows between these pairs, are small. The terminal object $1$ of $\mathcal C$ gives $(1,*)$ in $\mathcal N_p$. For $(T,a),(U,b)$, the element corresponding to $(a,b)$ in $L_p(T\times U)$ gives a common source. If $f,g:(T,a)\rightrightarrows(U,b)$ are parallel, then $L_p(f)(a)=L_p(g)(a)$; preservation of the equalizer $E\to T$ gives an element $e\in L_p(E)$ over $a$. The arrow $(E,e)\to(T,a)$ equalizes $f,g$. These are precisely the three cofilteredness conditions; hence $\mathcal N_p^{\mathrm{op}}$ is small filtered.

source.place: Tag 00YA (lemma-point-site-topos), proof of (2), finite-limit argument; Tag 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact); cofilteredness written out using products and equalizers

proof.text:
For every set $E$, the given adjunction, the universal property of sheafification, and Yoneda give natural bijections
$$(p_*E)(T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_T^\#,p_*E)\cong\operatorname{Map}(p^{-1}h_T^\#,E)=\operatorname{Map}(L_p(T),E).$$
For $b:T\to T'$, the restriction on the right is precomposition with $L_p(b)$. Indeed Yoneda is natural in $T$, and naturality of the adjunction carries precomposition with $h_b^\#$ to precomposition with $p^{-1}(h_b^\#)$. Thus the presheaf $T\mapsto\operatorname{Map}(L_p(T),E)$ is naturally the underlying presheaf of the already existing sheaf $p_*E$. No separate covering-surjectivity assertion is needed to establish that it is a sheaf.

source.place: Tag 00YA (2) and Tag 00Y8 (lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf): identify the skyscraper sheaf directly by the given adjunction and Yoneda

proof.text: For a sheaf of sets $H$, form $S(H)=\varinjlim_{(T,a)\in\mathcal N_p^{\mathrm{op}}}H(T)$ in sets (explicitly the disjoint union of the $H(T)$ labelled by $a$, modulo the relations $[T,a,s]=[U,c,H(b)s]$ for $b:(U,c)\to(T,a)$). A map $S(H)\to E$ is exactly a family of functions $\phi_{T,a}:H(T)\to E$ with $\phi_{T,a}(s)=\phi_{U,c}(H(b)s)$ for all such $b$. Currying this family gives $\tau_T:H(T)\to\operatorname{Map}(L_p(T),E)$ by $\tau_T(s)(a)=\phi_{T,a}(s)$. The compatibility just displayed is precisely the naturality equation for $\tau$. Step 2 identifies these natural transformations with sheaf morphisms $H\to p_*E$. Uncurrying reverses this construction. The colimit universal property therefore gives bijections $\operatorname{Map}(S(H),E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,p_*E)$ natural in $H,E$.

source.place: Tag 00Y7 (lemma-adjoint-point-push-stalk), explicit currying proof, together with the skyscraper identification in step 2

proof.text:
A section $s\in H(T)$ corresponds, by Yoneda and sheafification, to $s:h_T^\#\to H$. Define $c_H:S(H)\to p^{-1}H$ by $[T,a,s]\mapsto p^{-1}(s)(a)$. If $b:(U,c)\to(T,a)$, the restricted section is $s\circ h_b^\#$ and $L_p(b)(c)=a$, so functoriality makes the two images equal. For $v:p^{-1}H\to E$, its adjunct $H\to p_*E$, under step 2, sends $s$ to the function $a\mapsto v(p^{-1}(s)(a))$, by naturality of the adjunction in the map $s$. Hence the bijection of step 3 followed by the given adjunction is exactly precomposition with $c_H$:
$$\operatorname{Map}(p^{-1}H,E)\xrightarrow{\ c_H^*\ }\operatorname{Map}(S(H),E).$$
This proves $c_H$ invertible without an additional density assertion: for $E=S(H)$ choose $r:p^{-1}H\to S(H)$ with $r c_H=1$; injectivity of $c_H^*$ for $E=p^{-1}H$ gives $c_H r=1$. A map $H\to H'$ composes each section $s$ with that map, so the formula for $c_H$ also proves naturality in $H$.

source.place: Tag 00YA (lemma-point-site-topos), proof of (2), canonical comparison; bijectivity proved by the adjunction of Tag 00Y7 rather than the final coequalizer-presentation argument

proof.text: Now take $H$ to be the underlying sheaf of sets of $F$. Constant scalar sections give a $\Lambda$-module structure on every $F(T)$, with $\Lambda$-linear restriction maps. Let $M=\varinjlim_{\mathcal N_p^{\mathrm{op}}}F(T)$ in $\Lambda$-modules; existence follows from the cited module-colimit theorem. The set colimit $S(H)$ and the underlying set of $M$ are canonically bijective: both are covered by classes of pairs $((T,a),s)$, and in both, two classes are equal exactly when the two sections agree after maps to one common object of $\mathcal N_p^{\mathrm{op}}$, by the cited elementwise criteria. The bijection sends each section to its module-colimit class. Under it addition is computed after restricting two representatives to a common pointed object, and multiplication by a fixed $\lambda\in\Lambda$ is computed on one representative, since the module-colimit injections are linear.

source.place: Tag 00YA (2); Algebra Tags 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit) and 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit); Categories Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits)

proof.text: The cited constant-coefficient inverse-image theorem identifies the underlying set of $p^*_{\Lambda}F$ with $p^{-1}H$, its addition with $p^{-1}(+)$ using the finite-product comparison, and its scalar endomorphisms with the inverse images of those of $F$. Given two representatives in $M$, restrict them to a common $(T,a)$, where they are $s,t\in F(T)$. The section $(s,t):h_T^\#\to H\times H$ maps under $p^{-1}$ at $a$ to $(c_H[T,a,s],c_H[T,a,t])$, since its two projections are $s,t$. Composing with $+$ shows $c_H[T,a,s+t]=c_H[T,a,s]+c_H[T,a,t]$. The same composition argument with each scalar endomorphism gives $c_H[T,a,\lambda s]=\lambda c_H[T,a,s]$; zero is treated by the zero section. Step 5 therefore turns $c_H$ into the asserted bijective linear canonical map $M\to p^*_{\Lambda}F$. Its naturality follows from step 4 and the sectionwise action of module morphisms.

proof.text: The theorem on constant-coefficient inverse image applies to the geometric morphism $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, viewing $\mathbf{Set}$ as sheaves on the one-object point site. It gives exactness of $p^*_{\Lambda}$ directly. Independently $\mathcal N_p^{\mathrm{op}}$ is small filtered by step 1; the cited Grothendieck-abelian module theorem then gives exactness of colimits of arbitrary $\mathcal N_p^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagrams of $\Lambda$-modules. This does not assert that evaluation $F\mapsto F(T)$ sends a sheaf epimorphism to a surjection.

Let $i:\mathcal N'\hookrightarrow\mathcal N_p$ be a small full initial subcategory. Its initiality supplies an object over every object of $\mathcal N_p$. In particular it is nonempty. A common source in $\mathcal N_p$ of two objects of $\mathcal N'$ can be refined by an object of $\mathcal N'$; fullness puts the two composite arrows in $\mathcal N'$. An equalizing arrow in $\mathcal N_p$ for two parallel arrows of $\mathcal N'$ can likewise be refined from $\mathcal N'$, and fullness puts the composite equalizing arrow there. Thus $\mathcal N'$ is cofiltered. For the section diagram $D:\mathcal N_p^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda)$, regard its opposite as a diagram $D^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathcal N_p\to\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply the cited initial-functor limit theorem to $i$ and $D^{\mathrm{op}}$, then take opposites: the canonical map $\varinjlim_{\mathcal N'^{\mathrm{op}}}D i^{\mathrm{op}}\to\varinjlim_{\mathcal N_p^{\mathrm{op}}}D$ is an isomorphism. Its composite with step 6 has exactly the same representative formula. It is natural, and exactness of colimits on $\mathcal N'^{\mathrm{op}}$ follows again from the module theorem because this index is small filtered. The inverse-image functor is still the exact functor of step 7.
